newsitem.title: FRANCE: French seek confirmation of Iraq wheat deals.
newsitem.headline: French seek confirmation of Iraq wheat deals.

text.p: Iraq was said to have purchased between 300,000 and 325,000 tonnes of French wheat for March-April shipment but the deal was yet to be confirmed, European grain traders said on Tuesday.
"We are waiting for a confirmation. At the moment the Iraqis have not made any official announcement," one exporter said.
Iraq was seeking 100,000 tonnes of French wheat for March and April.
Exporters cited a selling price of $185.75 per tonne, cost and freight, for delivery to Umm Qasr, and $219 per tonne, cost and freight, for Baghdad through Jordan's port of Aqaba.
Iraq, which bought 300,000 tonnes of French wheat in December, has been negotiating a new purchase since January 14 under a U.N. oil-for-food plan.
U.N. officials said on Friday more than $100 million had been received in U.N. accounts set up to handle oil revenues raised under the renewable six-month deal.
